claims.claim: Michel characterises LLM output as probable-sounding but not necessarily accurate or even coherent.
claims.quote: probable-sounding but not necessarily accurate or even coherent
claims.page: opening section, after the two numbered assumptions

claims.claim: Michel states that the danger of LLMs for literature remains their quantity rather than their quality, and that he has never worried much about LLMs replacing authors on quality.
claims.quote: the danger of LLMs for literature remains their quantity, not their quality
claims.page: section 'The Slop Tsunami Could Still Drown Us Though'

claims.claim: Harvey Randall argues that background chatter, combat barks, NPC dialogue and side-quests all matter and are the backbone on which a game's story lies.
claims.source: Harvey Randall, staff writer, PC Gamer, 2026
claims.quote: Background chatter, combat barks, NPC dialogue, side-quests, it all matters.

claims.claim: Randall asserts that hand-written incidental lines such as combat barks characterise an enemy faction and journal entries flesh out a culture.
claims.source: Harvey Randall, staff writer, PC Gamer, 2026
claims.quote: Combat barks can characterise an enemy faction, journal entries can flesh out a culture

claims.claim: Randall argues that Starfield's procedurally generated planets and cities feel bland with all the rough edges sanded off next to New Vegas's hand-crafted background babble.
claims.source: Harvey Randall, staff writer, PC Gamer, 2026
claims.quote: all the rough edges sanded off

claims.feature: other: incidental detail builds scale and place
claims.claim: Randall asserts that a game's hundreds of small background lines can create a sense of scale or place rather than only conveying plot information.
claims.source: Harvey Randall, staff writer, PC Gamer, 2026
claims.quote: they can create a sense of scale or place

claims.claim: Adam Smith, Larian's writing director, said in a Reddit AMA that no text generation touches the dialogues, journal entries or other writing in Divinity.
claims.source: Adam Smith (Larian writing director) quoted by Ted Litchfield, PC Gamer, 2026
claims.quote: We don't have any text generation touching our dialogues, journal entries

claims.claim: Smith reported that Larian's experiments with text-generation tools produced results that hit a 3/10 at best, while his own worst first drafts are at least a 4/10.
claims.source: Adam Smith (Larian writing director) quoted by Ted Litchfield, PC Gamer, 2026
claims.quote: the results hit a 3/10 at best

claims.feature: other: sycophantic tone as a tell
claims.claim: Ted Litchfield writes that across Grok, Claude and ChatGPT people can never get the generative-AI stink off, a by turns smarmy and sycophantic tone.
claims.quote: a by turns smarmy and sycophantic tone
claims.page: reporter's aside after the AMA quotation

claims.feature: other: shaped like the thing but not the thing
claims.claim: David Gaider said BioWare's generated-quest experiments could make something shaped like a quest whose result was no better than a fetch quest.
claims.source: David Gaider (Dragon Age creator) tweeting, quoted by Robin Valentine, PC Gamer, 2023

claims.claim: Jonas Kyratzes, narrative designer on The Talos Principle 3, said in a Game Informer interview that he thinks the AI push is largely ludicrous.
claims.source: Jonas Kyratzes quoted from a Game Informer interview by Elie Gould, PC Gamer, 2026
claims.page: body, quoting the Game Informer interview

claims.claim: Wikipedia's WikiProject AI Cleanup explains the tells by statistical regression to the mean, which smooths specific facts into generic statements that could equally apply to many topics.
claims.source: WikiProject AI Cleanup, Wikipedia:Signs of AI writing, version of 6 September 2026
claims.quote: a smoothing over of specific facts into generic statements

claims.claim: The WikiProject holds that the model omits specific, unusual, nuanced facts because they are statistically rare and replaces them with generic positive descriptions.
claims.source: WikiProject AI Cleanup, Wikipedia:Signs of AI writing, version of 6 September 2026
claims.quote: tends to omit specific, unusual, nuanced facts

claims.feature: other: less specific and more exaggerated at once
claims.claim: The WikiProject states that in AI encyclopedic writing the subject becomes simultaneously less specific and more exaggerated.
claims.source: WikiProject AI Cleanup, Wikipedia:Signs of AI writing, version of 6 September 2026
claims.quote: The subject becomes simultaneously less specific and more exaggerated.

claims.claim: The WikiProject names as a tell that LLM writing puffs up the importance of the subject by adding statements about how arbitrary aspects represent or contribute to a broader topic.
claims.source: WikiProject AI Cleanup, Wikipedia:Signs of AI writing, version of 6 September 2026
claims.quote: LLM writing often puffs up the importance of the subject matter
claims.page: section 'Undue emphasis on significance, legacy, and broader trends'

verdicts.trueWording: They produce text that is probable-sounding but not necessarily accurate or even coherent.

Sentence appears verbatim in the paragraph immediately after the two numbered points (1) LLMs are nowhere close to becoming actual intelligences, 2) LLMs aren't going away), and the phrase is re-quoted in the next sentence.

verdicts.trueWording: I think the danger of LLMs for literature remains their quantity, not their quality.

Even my worst first drafts...are at least a 4/10.' Both numeric limbs supported.

Quoted fragment verbatim; the claim's paraphrase drops the page's hedge 'seem to' but no limb is unsupported.

verdicts.trueWording: something *shaped* like a quest... but the end result is no better than your typical 'bring me 20 beetle heads' MMO quest
verdicts.note: Raw page (curl, HTTP 200). Robin Valentine, PC Gamer, 30 May 2023. Quote verbatim (asterisks included) in the body, from Gaider's tweet reacting to a Guardian article; the article states BioWare 'went through several iterations' of procedural dialogue 'alongside procedural quests'. Two notes: the page frames the line as the core problem of 'any such system' rather than of BioWare's build alone, and 'fetch quest' is the claim's paraphrase of the page's 'bring me 20 beetle heads' MMO quest.

Raw page (curl, HTTP 200). Elie Gould, PC Gamer, 26 August 2026. Verbatim: "'I'm going to talk for myself,' Jonas Kyratzes, narrative designer, says in an interview with Game Informer. 'The AI push' is the claim's gloss of the antecedent 'it', which the page leaves to context but supports: he immediately calls 'the technology itself...very impressive' and elsewhere attacks 'excessive quasi-religious claims'.
